items.title: security: response-size guards buffer entire body before size check, unbounded for chunked/no-Content-Length responses
items.summary:
## Summary
The response-size guards in `OsvClient`, `PyPiMaintenanceRepository`, and `PyPiCompatibilityClient` still buffer the entire HTTP response body into memory via `response.bytes().await` before the post-download `bytes.len()` check runs, so a response with no `Content-Length` header (e.g. `Transfer-Encoding: chunked`) — or one that understates its own size — is not actually memory-bounded until after the full payload has already been received.

items.summary:
## 用户结果
柱状图里同一提供方的用量堆在一起（Claude / Codex / Gemini / 其他），而不是按机器；从标题下拉菜单能直接看到最近几期的总量对比。

## 验收
- 每根柱按 claude_tokens / codex_tokens / gemini_tokens / unknown_tokens 堆叠，Claude 在底；unknown 用 #8E8E93。
- 未来时段输出占位（无数值）。
- 期间菜单数据：日 7 / 周 6 / 月 6 期，每期总量 + 各提供方分量；**只读 SummaryCache 已有缓存**，缺失为「—」，
  展开菜单不触发任何网络请求。

## 红测建议
- 构造 trend 点，断言堆叠段顺序与数值守恒（段和 = 该点 tokens，独立复算）。
- 菜单数据：缓存命中 / 未命中各一例；断言未命中时 client 未被调用。

items.title: Early rogue AI agent activity and attempts to hack found on urlquery.net
items.summary: Liability only kicks in after damage has been done. As far as I know, there is no law that could currently force AI companies to only test cybersecurity capabilities in air-gapped datacenters, for example; only laws that could punish them if their cyber testing led to a hack that caused material damage. But if, lets say, a rogue AI agent swarm attacked a hospital and caused patients to die, no amount of liability will bring those patients back to life.

items.title: Revealing the details of how OpenAI agents hacked Hugging Face
items.summary: Agents should be a no-go. We should pause with AI/LLMs being super search engines that reply with static text or media files, based on the training data. I know that a user can still do a "tell me how to" then autoexec and then loop and do an agent, but the key thing here is, THAT WOULD MAKE THEM LIABLE. OpenAI should be criminally liable here as well. Why aren't they? Why are we pretending this is just an innocent mistake?
